steps.referenceSource: RE-FROZEN FOR THE CONTENT-BOX ITEM REGION FIX: layoutFlex, layoutGrid and layoutTable computed their item region by subtracting the container's own padding and border from element.box.width, which is already the content box, so every padded flex/grid/table container laid out up to 102px too narrow (djangoproject.com's header .container is display:flex with padding:0 4.16667%). The item region is now exactly `width`; innerX/innerY stay the border+padding content origin. The rule is Edge-verified on frozen fixtures in aurora-opencode-pro/build/browser-reference-validation-9 (flex-stretch-pad: a padded flex container stretches its item across its content box) and -13, and the real-page consequence is verified against an independent Edge frame captured this session at the same 1280x800, 1x (C:/Users/windows10/AppData/Local/Temp/aurora-evtest/django-edge-now.png). Both frames were measured with the same probe - the extent of light pixels inside x=30..420 of the dark green header band, whose page origin is y=138 in this capture: Edge header band page y=0..137, first text row page y=28..53, search field page y=76..121 at x=63..306; this engine now header band page y=0..132, text row page y=28..53, search field page y=76..121 at x=61..307. The superseded frame put the search field on the nav row under an 88px header and moved all page content 50px up, i.e. it encoded the defect; it is kept beside the new one as django29ref-pre-content-box-item-region.ppm. 195,963 of 1,024,000 pixels differ, nearly all of that the content shift below the header. KNOWN OPEN: the header band ends 5px higher than Edge's (133 vs 138), a line-box height difference of the substitute font stack, the same class of text-metric difference this document already records. AURORA-TO-AURORA REGRESSION BASELINE - NOT AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE. RE-FROZEN FOR THE BOX-SHADOW SPREAD FIX: pxLength now accepts a unitless zero, where `box-shadow: 10px 10px 0 0 #000` used to resolve its spread to -1 and inset the shadow by one pixel on every side. That changed exactly 79 of 1,024,000 pixels - row y=556, x=1..79, a one-pixel section divider that now starts at the viewport edge instead of 79px in. The shadow rule itself is Edge-verified in aurora-opencode-pro/build/browser-reference-validation-8/box-shadow.html (Aurora's shadow rectangle now matches Edge's 10,10,60,40 exactly); this real-page consequence is not independently verified, because a live page has no oracle - see aurora-browser/docs/browser-completion-profile.md. AURORA-TO-AURORA REGRESSION BASELINE - NOT AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE. Re-frozen again after the engine learned the CSS `font` shorthand, a formatting context root's auto height containing its floats (CSS 2.1 10.6.7), and U+00A0 no longer being treated as collapsible whitespace. That changed exactly 90 of 1,024,000 pixels: a 6x15 sliver of the scrollbar thumb at x=1272-1277, y=256-270, max channel delta 95, with every content pixel identical (measured with diff_ppm.py against the previous reference). The independent Edge corpus (browser-reference-validation-4, six frozen fixtures) passes every case, including the two float cases this change was made for. djangoproject.com at 1280x800, 1x device pixel ratio, captured from this engine; it can only detect a change, never prove correctness. The independent correctness oracle is the frozen Edge corpus in aurora-opencode-pro/build/browser-reference-validation/verify.json (box-model, flex-grid, svg-position, each with a manifest-pinned Edge reference), run as a second saved recipe. This baseline was re-frozen again when float placement learned CSS 9.5.1 (a float shifts beside, or drops below, the floats already active in its block formatting context), a float's auto height began including its floating descendants (CSS 10.6.7), and flex/grid/table containers began honouring margin collapsing through collapsedTopY and flow.hasPrevBlock. That last set changed exactly 6 of 1,024,000 pixels: a 6px sliver of the scrollbar thumb at x=1272-1277, y=271, because a float now measures 6px taller and the document with it. Both frames were inspected at full size and are visually identical; the independent Edge corpus (the oracle) passes every case. Earlier re-freeze: sha 9FC197B4... to E2AED91E... (3824 pixels, 0.4%) when resolveHeight stopped returning the border-box height for content-box sizing - the rule Edge validated in the box-model fixture (height:70px + padding:11 + border:7 must paint 156x106, not 156x142). The two frames were compared side by side and are visually identical: the difference is sub-visual edge shifts on the fundraiser card's broken-image placeholder. Expected content of the frame replaced above (it predates the content-box item-region fix and is superseded): header 72px tall, wordmark reading 'django', the menu OVERVIEW DOWNLOAD DOCUMENTATION NEWS CODE ISSUES COMMUNITY FOUNDATION <heart> DONATE SPONSOR on one line of bold uppercase 13px labels ending at x=1017 clear of the search field at x=1023; the hero tagline centred on two lines with the green 'Get started with Django' CTA centred beneath it (545,285 189x47); 'Meet Django' with its paragraph; the 'Download latest release: 6.1.2' card with 'Django documentation' 10px below it; 'Support Django!' with its fundraiser card. KNOWN OPEN: boqsc.eu's icon group has a pale rounded element behind it - that is the active page's own .site-toolbar__link background, i.e. intentional. RE-FROZEN FOR THE DEVICE-SCALE-EXPLICIT HEADLESS CAPTURE AND THE CSS FONT-FAMILY FIX: the probe is now compiled with -version=AuroraHeadless, so the frame it writes is exactly the requested logical size. It used to drive a real win32 window, whose framebuffer is logical x display scale, so at this machine's 125% display scale the same 1280x800 request wrote a 1600x1000 frame and this dimension check refused to compare it against the 1:1 reference; the app itself was correct there too (an independent Edge frame at the same 125% device scale, django-edge-125.png, puts the nav row and the search field at the engine's page coordinates). The headless frame is identical to the previous 1:1 window capture outside the page's text: the 138px of browser chrome and the header-band geometry match row for row, and every differing pixel sits in a text band (frame y=171..186, 224..242, 343..438, 468..551, 646..685, 708..775, plus 4 pixels on row 150). That is the font-family change: the engine used to shape every page in its own UI face and now resolves font-family/weight/style through the installed-font inventory, so a page that declares its family rasterises different glyphs. Layout did not move: measured with the same probe as Edge at 1280x800, 1x, this engine's header band is page y=0..132, its nav text row page y=28..53 and its search field page y=76..121 at x=61..307 against Edge's band 0..137, nav row 28..53 and search field 76..121 at x=63..306 (the 5px band height and the 2px x rounding stay known open, both recorded in aurora-browser/docs/rendering-status.md). The superseded frame is kept beside it as django29ref-pre-font-family.ppm. AURORA-TO-AURORA REGRESSION BASELINE - NOT AN INDEPENDENT ORACLE.
